note: Not assessable. This is an internal call between the closer and his setter with no prospect present, so there is nobody to judge against the ICP criteria; fit is left null rather than forced into core, edge or outside. The call is still relevant to the ICP question and should be read alongside the assessments rather than counted as one. It contains the clearest statement in the corpus of the income criterion being deliberately overridden: discussing a newly booked 23-year-old firefighter, the setter says 'the fact that he's 23 did make me question financial qualification a bit, but, as Chris was saying earlier, he was such a good fit, I thought I'd let it slide, and either way, I think we'll get him through on the primal year.' That is profile fit being traded against ability to pay at the setting stage, with a cheaper tier as the intended landing spot — which supports the existing observation that the buying population is wider than the stated ICP, and adds that the widening is deliberate and happens before the closer ever sees the lead.
